name: git-graffiti
description: Brute-force commit hashes by tweaking a hidden nonce until each hash prefix is whatever hex you want. git log --oneline then reads dead000 beef000 c0ffee0 or spells out hex art down the column.
readme_summary: Git-graffiti is a Rust tool that allows users to manipulate Git commit hashes by brute-forcing the SHA-1 algorithm to create custom prefixes. It achieves this by appending whitespace characters as a nonce to commit messages and then rewriting history to display these custom hashes, enabling the creation of hex art or specific hash patterns in the commit log.
key_features: Brute-force commit hashes to achieve custom prefixes.
Rewrite Git history with modified commit hashes.
Append whitespace (spaces and tabs) as a nonce for hash manipulation.
Utilize midstate caching and raw byte comparison for faster hashing.
Support for parallel processing within each commit's search (CPU/GPU).
Optional OpenCL GPU acceleration.
primary_use_case: To generate visually appealing or specific hexadecimal prefixes for Git commit hashes, enabling the creation of hex art or 'message-like' commit logs, despite the lack of practical utility.
cover_image_prompt: A whimsical, slightly mischievous wizard in a cluttered workshop, using a magical loom to weave threads of binary code into a tapestry. The tapestry displays a flowing Git commit graph, but instead of random hashes, the commits are clearly labeled with fun, recognizable hex patterns like 'c0ffee', 'bada55', and 'deadbeef'. The wizard is focused, with glowing runes around his hands and a subtle digital interface showing the 'nonce' being adjusted. The background has faint code snippets and Git logos. The overall mood is creative and playful, emphasizing the 'art' aspect of manipulating code. Style: 3D isometric illustration with vibrant, glowing colors and a clean, organized composition.

name: oh-my-mermaid
description: Turn complex codebases into clear, navigable architecture diagrams with Claude Code.
readme_summary: Oh-my-mermaid (omm) is a command-line tool that leverages AI to automatically generate architecture diagrams and documentation from complex codebases. It helps developers visualize and understand their code's structure, data flow, and integrations, transforming code into human-readable architecture documentation.
key_features: AI-powered codebase analysis
Automatic generation of architecture diagrams (Mermaid.js)
Hierarchical and recursive analysis of code structure
Generation of documentation fields (description, context, etc.)
Interactive viewer for exploring diagrams
CLI for setup, viewing, and configuration
Integration with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)
Cloud storage and sharing of architecture documentation
primary_use_case: To automatically generate and visualize software architecture documentation from codebases using AI, making complex systems easier to understand.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old librarian meticulously organizing a vast, chaotic library where the bookshelves are made of glowing code. The librarian uses a magical magnifying glass that, when pointed at a section of code-bookshelf, instantly transforms it into a clear, interconnected network of illuminated pathways and nodes, representing the architecture. Small, ethereal scrolls unfurl from the transformed code, displaying concise descriptions and diagrams. The scene is set in a cozy, dimly lit study with subtle digital particles floating in the air, hinting at the AI's involvement. The repository name 'oh-my-mermaid' is subtly etched onto the librarian's desk. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a warm, inviting color palette and clear, readable details.

name: FolderOrganizer
description: Automatically organize your files on Windows and Linux using customizable rules.
readme_summary: FolderOrganizer is an open-source application for Windows and Linux that automates file organization. It monitors specified directories and moves files into categorized folders based on customizable rules, file extensions, and predefined structures.
key_features: Automatic file organization
Customizable rules
File classification by extension
Automatic execution via Windows Service or systemd service
Manual execution option
Interactive configuration wizard
Language selection
Reuse of previous configurations
Validated Windows installer and Linux-compatible runtime
Open source
primary_use_case: Automating the organization of downloaded or miscellaneous files into predefined or custom-defined folder structures on Windows and Linux operating systems.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, anthropomorphic robot librarian diligently sorting a chaotic pile of diverse digital files (represented as colorful, distinct icons like documents, images, music notes, and code brackets) into perfectly organized, labeled shelves in a clean, modern digital library. Some files are flowing from a 'Downloads' cloud icon towards the robot. Subtle UI elements showing rule configurations and file extension icons are visible on a small holographic screen near the robot. The overall mood is efficient and tidy, with a soft, digital glow. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear, friendly character design and a vibrant, organized color palette.

name: quickemu
description: Quickly create and run optimised Windows, macOS and Linux virtual machines
readme_summary: Quickemu is a shell script wrapper for QEMU that simplifies the creation and management of optimized virtual machines for Windows, macOS, and various Linux distributions. It automates the download of operating systems and configures VMs with optimal settings for the host hardware, requiring minimal user intervention.
key_features: Automated OS downloads and VM configuration
Optimized VM settings based on host hardware
Support for Windows (including TPM 2.0), macOS, Linux, BSDs, and other OSs
ARM64 guest support
Full SPICE and VirtIO-webdavd/9p file sharing
QEMU Guest Agent support
VirGL acceleration
USB and Smartcard pass-through
EFI and Legacy BIOS boot support
primary_use_case: To quickly and easily create and run optimized virtual machines for various operating systems, including Windows and macOS, on Linux and macOS hosts.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, anthropomorphic robot assistant holding a magic wand, effortlessly assembling a complex, multi-layered digital castle representing a virtual machine. On one side, digital streams of code and OS logos (Windows, macOS, Linux Tux) flow into the wand. On the other side, the completed castle glows with internal lights, with small windows showing different operating systems running smoothly. Subtle UI elements and data particles surround the robot, hinting at automation. The scene is set in a clean, modern workshop with soft, inviting lighting. The style is a 3D isometric illustration with vibrant colors and clear, friendly character design, emphasizing ease of use and powerful functionality. The repository name 'Quickemu' is subtly etched on a nearby tool.

name: fastapi-silk
readme_summary: FastAPI-Silk is a lightweight middleware for FastAPI applications that profiles SQL queries executed through SQLAlchemy. It tracks query counts, database execution times, and total request times, providing this information via response headers and an interactive UI.
key_features: SQL instrumentation via SQLAlchemy engine events
Request-level metrics (X-DB-Queries, X-DB-Time, X-Total-Time headers)
Slow query logging to stdout
Per-request context isolation using contextvars
Minimal setup with one profiler call and middleware registration
Interactive UI for detailed profiling data
primary_use_case: To provide developers with detailed insights into the performance of SQL queries within their FastAPI applications, helping to identify and optimize slow database operations.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old librarian meticulously examining individual pages of ancient scrolls (representing SQL queries) that are flowing from a large, ornate pipe (representing the FastAPI application). Each scroll is illuminated, with some glowing red to indicate slowness, while others are a calm blue. The librarian is carefully noting down details on a ledger, showing query counts and timings. Subtle digital particles and faint code snippets float around the scene, hinting at the technological nature. The overall mood is one of focused analysis and optimization. The scene is set in a grand, dimly lit library with a clean, organized composition, rendered in a detailed digital painting style with clear outlines.
